request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: (patient's name)
Age: 84 years old
Gender: Female
Admission Date: (date of admission)
Discharge Date: (date of discharge)
Length of Stay: (number of days of hospital stay)
Clinical Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted due to her underlying medical conditions including type 2 diabetes and hypertension. She also had a history of amblyopia OD and a resolved branch retinal vein occlusion (BRVO) in the left eye. During her hospital stay, she was treated with Eyefolate™ capsules and no further complications were reported during the course of treatment.

Clinical Progress:
In October 2013, the patient's best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) was 20/150 OD and 20/25 OS. The OS fundus photo showed a large macular aneurysm (MA) in the superior temporal region with exudates. After being prescribed the Eyefolate™ capsules, the BCVA of the left eye improved to 20/20 in August 2014. Further improvement was seen in December 2014 when the large exudates almost completely resolved in OS (Fig. b). In January 2016, the BCVA was 20/400 OD and 20/25 OS, and the MA was resolved as shown in the OS fundus photo (Fig. c) during 2016.

Follow-up:
The patient was discharged in a stable condition with instructions to continue taking prescribed medications and regular follow-up appointments with her primary care physician to monitor her diabetes and hypertension. A referral to an ophthalmologist was also recommended to monitor her vision and perpetuate the effectiveness of the treatment.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The case centers on a retinal macular aneurysm (retinal macroaneurysm) with exudates in the left eye, after a prior branch retinal vein occlusion. The treatment was Eyefolate, and the visual outcomes concern the eye. The reason for admission is vaguely stated as underlying conditions, but the condition treated and followed is the retinal macroaneurysm.

In ICD-10, retinal aneurysm is not classed under a specific retinal vascular code in the H35 block, apart from H35.0 (background retinopathy and retinal vascular changes), which includes retinal aneurysm, so H35 is the likely category. The alternative is diabetic retinopathy (E11.3, with H36.0*), since the patient has type 2 diabetes. However, the macroaneurysm is typically attributed to hypertension, and the case does not call it diabetic retinopathy. The retinal macroaneurysm in H35.0 therefore fits best.

CODE: H35
